newsitem.title: UK: ICI shares surge 3.5 pct in pre-market.
newsitem.headline: ICI shares surge 3.5 pct in pre-market.

text.p: Shares in Imperial Chemical Industries opened pre-market trading 28 pence higher at 838-1/2 pence on Monday, after the company announced it had sold its industrial chemical operations to U.S. chemicals giant DuPont Co.
A trading update from the company was also greeted favourably by the stockmarket. ICI said it expected 1997 first half pretax profits of 160 million stg, before exceptional items.
"The price seems to be very fair. They have effectively divested of as much as they have to do," said Michael Eastwood, analyst at Kleinwort Benson.
"The profit before tax for the interim is in line with expectations. Although they still have a number of cyclical businesses with 40 percent of sales still not from speciality chemicals," he said.
The three billion dollar sale at ICI marks the shift in focus at the group from the bulk commodity chemicals area toward the higher margin speciality chemicals business.
The businesses to be sold to DuPont contributed total sales of 1.45 billion stg and trading profit of 17 million in 1996.
The three billion dollar sale completes ICI's restructuring under chief executive Charles Miller-Smith and expands DuPont's business in Europe.
"The deal looks very good. I think the speed of this deal will be taken especially well by the market," said one dealer, who chose not to be named.

ICI announced the acquisition of four speciality chemicals businesses from Unilever in early May. The sale to DuPont almost completes within three months the group's three year divestment target of three billion pounds against the original 4.9 billion stg cost buying the Unilever businesses.
The company's shares continued to move ahead in pre-market to show the biggest net gain of any stock, up 5.18 percent or 42-1/2 pence at 839-3/4p by 0720 GMT.
